title: An unramified algebra over a field is a finite product of finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra such that the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by the structure map [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then there are an integer $n\ge0$, fields $L_1,\dots,L_n$, each a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] which is finite ($\dim_kL_j<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $C\cong L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$ (for $n=0$ the zero ring). (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma [02G7] part (1), affine case; the same assertion appears in the proof of Algebra, Lemma [00UW] for the fibre ring $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of an unramified ring map.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (morphisms-lemma-unramified-over-field, line 7790), part (1), direction 'unramified implies disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions', applied to the affine scheme Spec C (quasi-compact, so finitely many points); also Algebra, Lemma 00UW (algebra-lemma-unramified-at-prime, algebra.tex line 41568), proof lines 41584-41591 ('F = S (x)_R kappa(p) is a finite product of finite separable field extensions of kappa(p)', via Algebra Lemmas 00UV (lemma-unramified), 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field) and 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field))
